indicator.name: Curiosity and Interest
indicator.description: Express interest in some familiar and new objects, people, and activities in their immediate environment. Seek information by exploring with their senses, describing their observations, and asking simple questions.

indicators.source_text:
Foundation 1.1 Curiosity and Interest
Early (3 to 4 ½ Years)
Express interest in some familiar and new objects, people, and activities in their immediate environment. Seek information by exploring with their senses, describing their observations, and asking simple questions.

indicator.name: Curiosity and Interest
indicator.description: Express interest in a broader range of familiar and new objects, people, and activities by exploring more extensively with their senses, describing their observations in greater detail, and asking more detailed questions.

indicators.source_text:
Foundation 1.1 Curiosity and Interest
Later (4 to 5 1/2 Years)
Express interest in a broader range of familiar and new objects, people, and activities by exploring more extensively with their senses, describing their observations in greater detail, and asking more detailed questions.

indicator.name: Initiative
indicator.description: Demonstrate initiative by starting activities (such as simple play scenarios), initiating social interactions (such as helping others), and seeking solutions to problems.

indicators.source_text:
Foundation 1.2 Initiative
Early (3 to 4 ½ Years)
Demonstrate initiative by starting activities (such as simple play scenarios), initiating social interactions (such as helping others), and seeking solutions to problems.

indicator.name: Initiative
indicator.description: Demonstrate initiative by starting activities (such as detailed and more complex play scenarios), initiating social interactions (such as helping others) more often, and seeking solutions to problems more persistently.

indicators.source_text:
Foundation 1.2 Initiative
Later (4 to 5 1/2 Years)
Demonstrate initiative by starting activities (such as detailed and more complex play scenarios), initiating social interactions (such as helping others) more often, and seeking solutions to problems more persistently.

indicator.name: Engagement
indicator.description: Actively engage by focusing and concentrating on activities for brief periods of time with adult support.

indicators.source_text:
Foundation 1.3 Engagement
Early (3 to 4 1/2 Years)
Actively engage by focusing and concentrating on activities for brief periods of time with adult support.

indicator.name: Engagement
indicator.description: Actively engage by focusing and concentrating on activities for longer periods of time with less adult support.

indicators.source_text:
Foundation 1.3 Engagement
Later (4 to 5 1/2 Years)
Actively engage by focusing and concentrating on activities for longer periods of time with less adult support.

indicator.name: Persisting Despite Difficulties
indicator.description: Demonstrate persistence, with adult support, when engaging in an activity despite encountering setbacks or boredom. Make an effort, with adult support, to cope with emotions that arise (for instance, frustration, anger, sadness, excitement), although may shift to another activity after a short while.

indicators.source_text:
Foundation 1.4 Persisting Despite Difficulties
Early (3 to 4 ½ Years)
Demonstrate persistence, with adult support, when engaging in an activity despite encountering setbacks or boredom. Make an effort, with adult support, to cope with emotions that arise (for instance, frustration, anger, sadness, excitement), although may shift to another activity after a short while.

indicator.name: Persisting Despite Difficulties
indicator.description: Demonstrate persistence for longer periods of time when engaging in an activity despite encountering setbacks or boredom. More consistently cope with emotions that arise (for instance, frustration, sadness, anger, excitement) and can continue engaging in an activity with less adult support.

indicators.source_text:
Foundation 1.4 Persisting Despite Difficulties
Later (4 to 5 ½ Years)
Demonstrate persistence for longer periods of time when engaging in an activity despite encountering setbacks or boredom. More consistently cope with emotions that arise (for instance, frustration, sadness, anger, excitement) and can continue engaging in an activity with less adult support.

indicator.name: Working Memory
indicator.description: Hold approximately one to two pieces of information in their mind for a short time and use the knowledge to guide behavior when performing tasks and engaging in play, with adult support.

indicators.source_text:
Foundation 2.1 Working Memory
Early (3 to 4 ½ Years)
Hold approximately one to two pieces of information in their mind for a short time and use the knowledge to guide behavior when performing tasks and engaging in play, with adult support.

indicator.name: Working Memory
indicator.description: Hold approximately two to three pieces of information in their mind for longer periods of time and use the knowledge to guide behavior when engaging in multistep tasks and more complex play, with less adult support.

indicators.source_text:
Foundation 2.1 Working Memory
Later (4 to 5 ½ Years)
Hold approximately two to three pieces of information in their mind for longer periods of time and use the knowledge to guide behavior when engaging in multistep tasks and more complex play, with less adult support.

indicator.name: Managing Impulsive Behaviors
indicator.description: Demonstrate emerging ability to manage habitual reactions (habits that are not useful in a particular context), impulsive behaviors (acting on a whim), and delaying gratification (resisting temptation for an instant reward) with adult support.

indicators.source_text:
Foundation 2.2 Managing Impulsive Behaviors
Early (3 to 4 1/2 Years)
Demonstrate emerging ability to manage habitual reactions (habits that are not useful in a particular context), impulsive behaviors (acting on a whim), and delaying gratification (resisting temptation for an instant reward) with adult support.

indicator.name: Managing Impulsive Behaviors
indicator.description: Manage habitual reactions (habits that are not useful in a particular context), impulsive behaviors (acting on a whim), and delaying gratification (resisting temptation for an instant reward) with less adult support.

indicators.source_text:
Foundation 2.2 Managing Impulsive Behaviors
Later (4 to 5 1/2 Years)
Manage habitual reactions (habits that are not useful in a particular context), impulsive behaviors (acting on a whim), and delaying gratification (resisting temptation for an instant reward) with less adult support.

indicator.name: Managing Attention and Distractions
indicator.description: Demonstrate an emerging ability to ignore distractions and interruptions during independent or group activities; however, often need adult support to manage attention when distracted or interrupted.

indicators.source_text:
Foundation 2.3 Managing Attention and Distractions
Early (3 to 4 ½ Years)
Demonstrate an emerging ability to ignore distractions and interruptions during independent or group activities; however, often need adult support to manage attention when distracted or interrupted.

indicator.name: Managing Attention and Distractions
indicator.description: Demonstrate an emerging ability to ignore distractions and interruptions during independent or group activities with less adult support.

indicators.source_text:
Foundation 2.3 Managing Attention and Distractions
Later (4 to 5 ½ Years)
Demonstrate an emerging ability to ignore distractions and interruptions during independent or group activities with less adult support.

indicator.name: Flexibility
indicator.description: Demonstrate emerging ability to shift behavior and think about things in a new way, with adult support.

indicators.source_text:
Foundation 2.4 Flexibility
Early (3 to 4 1/2 Years)
Demonstrate emerging ability to shift behavior and think about things in a new way, with adult support.

indicator.name: Flexibility
indicator.description: More consistently shift behavior and think about things in a new way, with less adult support.

indicators.source_text:
Foundation 2.4 Flexibility
Later (4 to 5 1/2 Years)
More consistently shift behavior and think about things in a new way, with less adult support.

indicator.name: Planning
indicator.description: Demonstrate emerging ability to set and carry out simple goals (for example, one- to two-step plans and goals), with adult support.

indicators.source_text:
Foundation 3.1 Planning
Early (3 to 4 1/2 Years)
Demonstrate emerging ability to set and carry out simple goals (for example, one- to two-step plans and goals), with adult support.

indicator.name: Planning
indicator.description: Demonstrate ability to set and carry out more complex plans (for example, two- to three-step plans and goals), with less adult support.

indicators.source_text:
Foundation 3.1 Planning
Later (4 to 5 1/2 Years)
Demonstrate ability to set and carry out more complex plans (for example, two- to three-step plans and goals), with less adult support.

indicator.name: Reflecting and Analyzing
indicator.description: Make attempts to adjust a problem-solving approach or strategy by reflecting on and analyzing their current approach, with adult support.

indicators.source_text:
Foundation 3.2 Reflecting and Analyzing
Early (3 to 4 1/2 Years)
Make attempts to adjust a problem-solving approach or strategy by reflecting on and analyzing their current approach, with adult support.

indicator.name: Reflecting and Analyzing
indicator.description: Make attempts to adjust a problem-solving approach or strategy by reflecting on and analyzing their current approach, with less adult support.

indicators.source_text:
Foundation 3.2 Reflecting and Analyzing
Later (4 to 5 1/2 Years)
Make attempts to adjust a problem-solving approach or strategy by reflecting on and analyzing their current approach, with less adult support.

indicator.name: Problem-Solving Together
indicator.description: Collaborate with peers in problem-solving during play and learning activities, sometimes for a short period of time and sometimes longer.

indicators.source_text:
Foundation 3.3 Problem-Solving Together
Early (3 to 4 ½ Years)
Collaborate with peers in problem-solving during play and learning activities, sometimes for a short period of time and sometimes longer.

indicator.name: Problem-Solving Together
indicator.description: Engage in extended collaborative problem-solving during play and learning activities. Communicate with peers about how to solve a problem and help peers when needed.

indicators.source_text:
Foundation 3.3 Problem-Solving Together
Later (4 to 5 ½ Years)
Engage in extended collaborative problem-solving during play and learning activities. Communicate with peers about how to solve a problem and help peers when needed.

indicator.name: Understanding Others
indicator.description: Notice, with adult support, that others have different approaches and preferences, although often have difficulty accepting others' approaches or preferences.

indicators.source_text:
Foundation 3.4 Understanding Others
Early (3 to 4 ½ Years)
Notice, with adult support, that others have different approaches and preferences, although often have difficulty accepting others' approaches or preferences.

indicator.name: Understanding Others
indicator.description: Demonstrate understanding and explain that others can have different approaches and preferences and more consistently accept others' approaches and preferences, with less adult support.

indicators.source_text:
Foundation 3.4 Understanding Others
Later (4 to 5 1/2 Years)
Demonstrate understanding and explain that others can have different approaches and preferences and more consistently accept others' approaches and preferences, with less adult support.

domain.name: Foundational Language Development
domain.description: This is one out of two sub-domains in the Language and Literacy Development domain.

indicator.name: Understanding and Using Vocabulary
indicator.description: Understand and use words for objects, actions, and attributes frequently experienced in everyday life, such as through play, conversations, or stories.

indicators.source_text:
Foundation 1.1 Understanding and Using Vocabulary
Early (3 to 4 ½ Years)
Understand and use words for objects, actions, and attributes frequently experienced in everyday life, such as through play, conversations, or stories.

domain.name: Foundational Language Development
domain.description: This is one out of two sub-domains in the Language and Literacy Development domain.

indicator.name: Understanding and Using Vocabulary
indicator.description: Understand and use an increasing variety of words for objects, actions, and attributes experienced in everyday life, such as through play, conversations, or stories.

indicators.source_text:
Foundation 1.1 Understanding and Using Vocabulary
Later (4 to 5 1/2 Years)
Understand and use an increasing variety of words for objects, actions, and attributes experienced in everyday life, such as through play, conversations, or stories.

domain.name: Foundational Language Development
domain.description: This is one out of two sub-domains in the Language and Literacy Development domain.

indicator.name: Understanding and Using Words for Categories
indicator.description: Understand and use commonly experienced vocabulary to describe categories and the relationships within them.

indicators.source_text:
Foundation 1.2 Understanding and Using Words for Categories
Early (3 to 4 1/2 Years)
Understand and use commonly experienced vocabulary to describe categories and the relationships within them.

domain.name: Foundational Language Development
domain.description: This is one out of two sub-domains in the Language and Literacy Development domain.

indicator.name: Understanding and Using Words for Categories
indicator.description: Understand and use increasingly specific vocabulary to describe categories and the relationships within them.

indicators.source_text:
Foundation 1.2 Understanding and Using Words for Categories
Later (4 to 5 ½ Years)
Understand and use increasingly specific vocabulary to describe categories and the relationships within them.

domain.name: Foundational Language Development
domain.description: This is one out of two sub-domains in the Language and Literacy Development domain.

indicator.name: Understanding and Using Size and Location Words
indicator.description: Understand and use words to describe the size and location of objects (such as "tiny" and "on"), including simple comparisons (such as "bigger").

indicators.source_text:
Foundation 1.3 Understanding and Using Size and Location Words
Early (3 to 4 ½ Years)
Understand and use words to describe the size and location of objects (such as "tiny" and "on"), including simple comparisons (such as "bigger").

domain.name: Foundational Language Development
domain.description: This is one out of two sub-domains in the Language and Literacy Development domain.

indicator.name: Understanding and Using Size and Location Words
indicator.description: Understand and use increasingly specific words to describe and compare the size and location of objects (such as "longer" and "between").

indicators.source_text:
Foundation 1.3 Understanding and Using Size and Location Words
Later (4 to 5 ½ Years)
Understand and use increasingly specific words to describe and compare the size and location of objects (such as "longer" and "between").

domain.name: Foundational Language Development
domain.description: This is one out of two sub-domains in the Language and Literacy Development domain.

indicator.name: Using Grammatical Features and Sentence Structure
indicator.description: Use common word forms and sentence forms to express thoughts and ideas.

indicators.source_text:
Foundation 1.4 Using Grammatical Features and Sentence Structure*
Early (3 to 4 ½ Years)
Use common word forms and sentence forms to express thoughts and ideas.

domain.name: Foundational Language Development
domain.description: This is one out of two sub-domains in the Language and Literacy Development domain.

indicator.name: Using Grammatical Features and Sentence Structure
indicator.description: Use both common and less common word forms and sentence forms to express complex thoughts and ideas.

indicators.source_text:
Foundation 1.4 Using Grammatical Features and Sentence Structure*
Later (4 to 5 1/2 Years)
Use both common and less common word forms and sentence forms to express complex thoughts and ideas.

domain.name: Foundational Language Development
domain.description: This is one out of two sub-domains in the Language and Literacy Development domain.

indicator.name: Asking Questions
indicator.description: Use questions to seek information and to clarify and confirm understanding.

indicators.source_text:
Foundation 1.5 Asking Questions
Early (3 to 4 ½ Years)
Use questions to seek information and to clarify and confirm understanding.

domain.name: Foundational Language Development
domain.description: This is one out of two sub-domains in the Language and Literacy Development domain.

indicator.name: Asking Questions
indicator.description: Use questions and follow-up questions to seek information and to clarify and confirm understanding.

indicators.source_text:
Foundation 1.5 Asking Questions
Later (4 to 5 ½ Years)
Use questions and follow-up questions to seek information and to clarify and confirm understanding.

domain.name: Foundational Language Development
domain.description: This is one out of two sub-domains in the Language and Literacy Development domain.

indicator.name: Constructing Narratives
indicator.description: Use language to construct real or fictional short narratives.

indicators.source_text:
Foundation 1.6 Constructing Narratives
Early (3 to 4 ½ Years)
Use language to construct real or fictional short narratives.

domain.name: Foundational Language Development
domain.description: This is one out of two sub-domains in the Language and Literacy Development domain.

indicator.name: Constructing Narratives
indicator.description: Use language to construct real or fictional extended narratives that have several details or a plotline.

indicators.source_text:
Foundation 1.6 Constructing Narratives
Later (4 to 5 ½ Years)
Use language to construct real or fictional extended narratives that have several details or a plotline.

domain.name: Foundational Language Development
domain.description: This is one out of two sub-domains in the Language and Literacy Development domain.

indicator.name: Sharing Explanations and Opinions
indicator.description: Share descriptions, opinions, and explanations.

indicators.source_text:
Foundation 1.7 Sharing Explanations and Opinions
Early (3 to 4 1/2 Years)
Share descriptions, opinions, and
explanations.

domain.name: Foundational Language Development
domain.description: This is one out of two sub-domains in the Language and Literacy Development domain.

indicator.name: Sharing Explanations and Opinions
indicator.description: Share detailed descriptions, opinions, and explanations.

indicators.source_text:
Foundation 1.7 Sharing Explanations and Opinions
Later (4 to 5 1/2 Years)
Share detailed descriptions, opinions, and
explanations.

domain.name: Foundational Language Development
domain.description: This is one out of two sub-domains in the Language and Literacy Development domain.

indicator.name: Participating in Conversations
indicator.description: Participate in back-and-forth conversations with adults and peers. Respond on topic for at least one turn in a conversation.

indicators.source_text:
Foundation 1.8 Participating in Conversations
Early (3 to 4 1/2 Years)
Participate in back-and-forth conversations
with adults and peers. Respond on topic for at
least one turn in a conversation.

domain.name: Foundational Language Development
domain.description: This is one out of two sub-domains in the Language and Literacy Development domain.

indicator.name: Participating in Conversations
indicator.description: Participate in increasingly long and complex back-and-forth conversations with adults and peers. Respond on topic across several turns in the conversation.

indicators.source_text:
Foundation 1.8 Participating in Conversations
Later (4 to 5 ½ Years)
Participate in increasingly long and complex
back-and-forth conversations with adults and
peers. Respond on topic across several turns
in the conversation.

domain.name: Foundational Language Development
domain.description: This is one out of two sub-domains in the Language and Literacy Development domain.

indicator.name: Isolating Initial Sounds
indicator.description: Match words that have the same first sound in speech, with adult support or the support of pictures or objects.

indicators.source_text:
Foundation 2.1 Isolating Initial Sounds
Early (3 to 4 ½ Years)
Match words that have the same first sound in
speech, with adult support or the support of
pictures or objects.

domain.name: Foundational Language Development
domain.description: This is one out of two sub-domains in the Language and Literacy Development domain.

indicator.name: Isolating Initial Sounds
indicator.description: Isolate and pronounce the first sound of a word, with adult support or the support of pictures or objects.

indicators.source_text:
Foundation 2.1 Isolating Initial Sounds
Later (4 to 5 ½ Years)
Isolate and pronounce the first sound of a
word, with adult support or the support of
pictures or objects.

domain.name: Foundational Language Development
domain.description: This is one out of two sub-domains in the Language and Literacy Development domain.

indicator.name: Recognizing and Blending Sounds
indicator.description: When presented with two single-syllable words (such as "sand" and "box"), blend them into a compound word in speech with adult support or the support of pictures or objects.

indicators.source_text:
Foundation 2.2 Recognizing and Blending Sounds*
Early (3 to 4 ½ Years)
When presented with two single-syllable
words (such as "sand" and "box"), blend them
into a compound word in speech with adult
support or the support of pictures or objects.

domain.name: Foundational Language Development
domain.description: This is one out of two sub-domains in the Language and Literacy Development domain.

indicator.name: Recognizing and Blending Sounds
indicator.description: When presented with syllables and individual sounds, blend them into words in speech with adult support or the support of pictures or objects.

indicators.source_text:
Foundation 2.2 Recognizing and Blending Sounds*
Later (4 to 5 ½ Years)
When presented with syllables and individual
sounds, blend them into words in speech with
adult support or the support of pictures or
objects.

domain.name: Foundational Language Development
domain.description: This is one out of two sub-domains in the Language and Literacy Development domain.

indicator.name: Participating in Rhyming and Wordplay
indicator.description: Recognize or participate in familiar rhymes or songs.

indicators.source_text:
Foundation 2.3 Participating in Rhyming and Wordplay
Early (3 to 4 1/2 Years)
Recognize or participate in familiar rhymes or
songs.

domain.name: Foundational Language Development
domain.description: This is one out of two sub-domains in the Language and Literacy Development domain.

indicator.name: Participating in Rhyming and Wordplay
indicator.description: Produce rhyming sounds or words. Rhymes may be imperfect and can be real or nonsense words.

indicators.source_text:
Foundation 2.3 Participating in Rhyming and Wordplay
Later (4 to 5 1/2 Years)
Produce rhyming sounds or words. Rhymes
may be imperfect and can be real or nonsense
words.

domain.name: English Language Development
domain.description: This is one out of two sub-domains in the Language and Literacy Development domain.

indicator.name: Understanding Words
indicator.description: Pay attention to English oral language and understand a few common English words, while relying mainly on intonation, facial expressions, and gestures of the speaker in interactions with adults and peers.

indicators.source_text:
Foundation 1.1 Understanding Words
Discovering
Pay attention to English oral
language and understand
a few common English
words, while relying
mainly on intonation, facial
expressions, and gestures of
the speaker in interactions
with adults and peers.

domain.name: English Language Development
domain.description: This is one out of two sub-domains in the Language and Literacy Development domain.

indicator.name: Understanding Words
indicator.description: Demonstrate understanding of words in English for objects and actions as well as phrases encountered frequently in interactions with adults and peers.

indicators.source_text:
Developing
Demonstrate understanding
of words in English for
objects and actions as well
as phrases encountered
frequently in interactions
with adults and peers.

domain.name: English Language Development
domain.description: This is one out of two sub-domains in the Language and Literacy Development domain.

indicator.name: Understanding Words
indicator.description: Demonstrate understanding of a larger set of words in English (for example, objects and actions, personal pronouns, possessives, and descriptive terms) in interactions with adults and peers.

indicators.source_text:
Broadening
Demonstrate understanding
of a larger set of words
in English (for example,
objects and actions, personal
pronouns, possessives,
and descriptive terms) in
interactions with adults and
peers.

domain.name: English Language Development
domain.description: This is one out of two sub-domains in the Language and Literacy Development domain.

indicator.name: Using Words
indicator.description: Use English words, mainly consisting of concrete nouns.

indicators.source_text:
Foundation 1.2 Using Words
Discovering
Use English words, mainly
consisting of concrete nouns.

domain.name: English Language Development
domain.description: This is one out of two sub-domains in the Language and Literacy Development domain.

indicator.name: Using Words
indicator.description: Use varied English words, including an increasing number of concrete nouns and some verbs and pronouns.

indicators.source_text:
Developing
Use varied English words,
including an increasing
number of concrete nouns
and some verbs and
pronouns.

domain.name: English Language Development
domain.description: This is one out of two sub-domains in the Language and Literacy Development domain.

indicator.name: Using Words
indicator.description: Use a wide variety of English words to share knowledge of concepts, including words across all parts of speech, with some inaccuracies.

indicators.source_text:
Broadening
Use a wide variety of English
words to share knowledge
of concepts, including words
across all parts of speech,
with some inaccuracies.

domain.name: English Language Development
domain.description: This is one out of two sub-domains in the Language and Literacy Development domain.

indicator.name: Using Grammatical Features
indicator.description: Use one or two familiar English verbs as all-purpose verbs, with some inaccuracies.

indicators.source_text:
Foundation 1.3 Using Grammatical Features
Discovering
Use one or two familiar
English verbs as all-
purpose verbs, with some
inaccuracies.

domain.name: English Language Development
domain.description: This is one out of two sub-domains in the Language and Literacy Development domain.

indicator.name: Using Grammatical Features
indicator.description: Use some grammatical rules in English, such as using -S or -es for plural nouns and -ing for verbs, sometimes with inaccuracies.

indicators.source_text:
Developing
Use some grammatical rules
in English, such as using -S or
-es for plural nouns and -ing
for verbs, sometimes with
inaccuracies.

domain.name: English Language Development
domain.description: This is one out of two sub-domains in the Language and Literacy Development domain.

indicator.name: Using Grammatical Features
indicator.description: Broaden the use of English grammatical rules, such as irregular plurals or simple past tense verbs, sometimes with inaccuracies.

indicators.source_text:
Broadening
Broaden the use of English
grammatical rules, such as
irregular plurals or simple
past tense verbs, sometimes
with inaccuracies.

domain.name: English Language Development
domain.description: This is one out of two sub-domains in the Language and Literacy Development domain.

indicator.name: Using Complex Sentence Structures
indicator.description: Use words or phrases repeatedly experienced in English to communicate.

indicators.source_text:
Foundation 1.4 Using Complex Sentence Structures
Discovering
Use words or phrases
repeatedly experienced in
English to communicate.

domain.name: English Language Development
domain.description: This is one out of two sub-domains in the Language and Literacy Development domain.

indicator.name: Using Complex Sentence Structures
indicator.description: Use a few formulaic English grammatical forms, with some inaccuracies, to produce many different types of sentence structures.

indicators.source_text:
Developing
Use a few formulaic English
grammatical forms, with
some inaccuracies, to
produce many different
types of sentence structures.

domain.name: English Language Development
domain.description: This is one out of two sub-domains in the Language and Literacy Development domain.

indicator.name: Using Complex Sentence Structures
indicator.description: Use a variety of English sentence structures to communicate on a range of topics by switching out key words in a phrase. Grammatical forms can include adding appropriate possessive pronouns (for example, your, my); conjunctions (for example, and, or); and other elements (for example, adjectives, adverbs).

indicators.source_text:
Broadening
Use a variety of English
sentence structures to
communicate on a range of
topics by switching out key
words in a phrase.
Grammatical forms can
include adding appropriate
possessive pronouns
(for example, your, my);
conjunctions (for example,
and, or); and other elements
(for example, adjectives,
adverbs).

domain.name: English Language Development
domain.description: This is one out of two sub-domains in the Language and Literacy Development domain.

indicator.name: Communicating Needs
indicator.description: Combine nonverbal communication and some English phrases to be understood by English speakers.

indicators.source_text:
Foundation 1.5 Communicating Needs
Discovering
Combine nonverbal
communication and some
English phrases to be
understood by English
speakers.

domain.name: English Language Development
domain.description: This is one out of two sub-domains in the Language and Literacy Development domain.

indicator.name: Communicating Needs
indicator.description: Use single English words and nonverbal communication with English speakers, such as gestures or behaviors, to seek attention, make a request, or initiate a response.

indicators.source_text:
Developing
Use single English words and
nonverbal communication
with English speakers, such
as gestures or behaviors,
to seek attention, make
a request, or initiate a
response.

domain.name: English Language Development
domain.description: This is one out of two sub-domains in the Language and Literacy Development domain.

indicator.name: Communicating Needs
indicator.description: Show increasing reliance on verbal communication in English to be understood by English speakers.

indicators.source_text:
Broadening
Show increasing reliance on
verbal communication in
English to be understood by
English speakers.

domain.name: English Language Development
domain.description: This is one out of two sub-domains in the Language and Literacy Development domain.

indicator.name: Understanding Requests and Directions
indicator.description: Follow directions in English that involve repeatedly experienced routines or contextual clues.

indicators.source_text:
Foundation 1.6 Understanding Requests and Directions
Discovering
Follow directions in English
that involve repeatedly
experienced routines or
contextual clues.

domain.name: English Language Development
domain.description: This is one out of two sub-domains in the Language and Literacy Development domain.

indicator.name: Understanding Requests and Directions
indicator.description: Follow simple directions in English when given additional contextual clues.

indicators.source_text:
Developing
Follow simple directions
in English when given
additional contextual clues.

domain.name: English Language Development
domain.description: This is one out of two sub-domains in the Language and Literacy Development domain.

indicator.name: Understanding Requests and Directions
indicator.description: Follow directions that involve more than one step, relying less on contextual clues.

indicators.source_text:
Broadening
Follow directions that involve
more than one step, relying
less on contextual clues.

domain.name: English Language Development
domain.description: This is one out of two sub-domains in the Language and Literacy Development domain.

indicator.name: Asking Questions
indicator.description: Use a few question structures as a formula, filling in different words to ask about various topics.

indicators.source_text:
Foundation 1.7 Asking Questions
Discovering
Use a few question
structures as a formula,
filling in different words to
